clue.text: No overtaking, perhaps, as horseboxes like to hog lanes in the end

indicators.note: boxes is a verb here: the horse word encloses everything that follows it

parts.note: a roan is a horse with a coat flecked with white or grey

indicators.note: to hog something is to keep it to yourself, so the word for like holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: to dig something is slang for liking it

indicators.note: in the end points to the final letter of the word lanes

explanation.surface: A complaint that slow horse trailers sit in the middle of the road where nobody can get past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horseboxes' must be split in two: 'horse' is the outer piece and 'boxes' signals it enclosing the rest; 'like to hog' then has the like word hold the final S. The surface's slow horse trailers are a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: A No Overtaking notice is one example of the signs posted beside a highway for drivers.

clue.text: Low point to shake that booty!

definitions.meaning: the lowest level something can reach
slang for dancing: to rock one's backside

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the lowest possible level, and read as verb plus noun it means wiggling one's backside.

clue.text: Dreadful stain baby's left by tap — there's no baby-wetter!

indicators.note: dreadful suggests something badly done, so these letters are jumbled
left takes the left half of the word baby

explanation.surface: A complaint that a baby has left a horrible stain near the tap, not a drip from a nappy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' gives the left half of BABY, BA; 'Dreadful' rearranges STAIN, BA and TAP together.
explanation.definitionFit: This Protestant sect rejects infant baptism, so no member would wet a baby at the font.

clue.text: Observation of mating bull in market as judge of talent

indicators.note: in places the bull's remark inside the market word

parts.note: to market something is to sell it
a mating bull might observe I'm on cow

explanation.surface: A remark at a cattle market about watching a bull mate, with a judge assessing the stock.
explanation.walkthrough: The bull would say 'I'm on cow', and that goes inside SELL.
explanation.definitionFit: Simon Cowell is the television talent-show judge known from The X Factor and Britain's Got Talent.

clue.text: Playwright after amateur actor in relative, no straight man

indicators.note: after puts the playwright following the rest
in places the actor word inside the relative word

parts.note: a gran is a grandmother, a relative
a ham is an overacting or amateurish performer
Joe Orton was an English playwright

explanation.surface: A theatrical bit about a playwright following an amateur actor in a family drama, with no comic foil.
explanation.walkthrough: Graham Norton is an openly gay Irish TV chat-show host, hence 'no straight man', which also plays on the comedy term.
explanation.definitionFit: The chat-show host is openly gay, so he is literally not straight, and as a comic he is no stooge.

clue.text: Burn nearly 20 in front of church

indicators.note: in front of places the shortened twenty before the church letters
nearly means the word is not quite complete, losing its last letter

parts.note: a score is twenty

explanation.surface: An instruction for a recipe or a ritual: burn something just shy of twenty items before going to church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' drops the last letter of SCORE to give SCOR.
explanation.definitionFit: To scorch is to burn the surface of something, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Clear middle note, as piano is to pianoforte?

parts.note: middle C is the note in the middle of the keyboard
forte means loud, so piano is pianoforte with loud taken away

explanation.surface: A musical riddle comparing a piano to its full name.
explanation.walkthrough: PIANOFORTE minus FORTE, Italian for loud, leaves PIANO: so piano is pianoforte 'loud-less'.
explanation.definitionFit: A clear sky has no clouds at all, so it is cloudless.

clue.text: One can't take off part of cylinder head

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A mechanic's complaint about a part of an engine that won't come off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take off' suggests unscrewing an engine part; it means flying.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhea is a large South American bird that cannot fly, so it never takes off.

clue.text: See 23
Starter of bass in stuff to consume as seafood

indicators.note: in places the first letter of bass inside the word for stuff

parts.note: to cram is to stuff something full

indicators.note: starter of means only the opening letter of bass is used

parts.note: to eat is to consume food

explanation.surface: Advice on how to pack a dish with bass for the opening course and then eat it as seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: Crab meat is the edible flesh of crabs, a kind of shellfish served as seafood.

clue.text: See 3
Current problem, revolutio?

definitions.meaning: a fault in an electrical current
the word revolution with its last letter cut off: a circuit made short

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names an electrical fault; a revolution is a circuit, and revolutio is one shortened.

clue.text: Angelina's man's packed in — could he have been indoctrinated?

indicators.note: packed means the actor's name has the next words stuffed inside it

parts.note: Brad Pitt was famously Angelina Jolie's partner; the 's reads as has
taken as written
the question could he have been is turned into the words was he, used as letters

explanation.surface: A gossip-column aside: Angelina's partner has quit, so was he brainwashed into leaving?
explanation.walkthrough: BRAD (Pitt, Angelina Jolie's husband) has IN and WAS HE packed inside him. 'could he have been' stands for the question 'was he?'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone brainwashed has had beliefs forced into their mind, which is what indoctrinated describes.

clue.text: Give jellied eels in rice

indicators.note: jellied suggests something set into a new shape, so these letters are remade

explanation.surface: A recipe suggestion: serve jellied eels on rice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jellied' rearranges EELS IN RICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Give, as a noun, is springiness or elasticity, the ability to bounce back that resilience names.

clue.text: A cord with net designed to be tough

parts.note: a cord is a piece of string

indicators.note: designed means the letters are arranged into a new pattern

explanation.surface: Instructions for a strong mesh made from a cord and a net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges NET into ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Astringent means harsh or severe, a stern sense of tough.

clue.text: Tax man after fool

indicators.note: after puts the man word following the fool word

parts.note: tit is a slang word for a foolish person
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: The taxman comes along behind some idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe is a tax, historically one tenth of produce paid to support the church.

clue.text: Bloody woman holding heads of people and lowering beneath river, perfect

indicators.note: beneath in a down clue puts the woman's name below the river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon

indicators.note: holding means the woman's name contains the picked letters

parts.note: Mary I of England was nicknamed Bloody Mary

indicators.note: heads of takes the first letters of people and lowering

explanation.surface: A grim historical tableau of a queen lifting heads from a river.
explanation.walkthrough: MARY holds P and L, giving MPLARY, under EXE, a river in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Exemplary means serving as a model, ideal and faultless, so perfect.

clue.text: Cold figure returning to grab last of winter smalls, individually

indicators.note: to grab means the reversed number takes hold of a letter inside it
returning means the number word is read backwards

parts.note: a figure is a number, here eleven

indicators.note: last of takes only the final letter of winter

parts.note: smalls are underwear, and individually means each is taken as a single small, S, twice

explanation.surface: A chilly picture of someone turning back to snatch the last of their winter underwear one piece at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns ELEVEN into NEVELE, which grabs R; SMALLS is British for underwear, and S is small, so two S's follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerveless means calm and unflustered, the cool composure suggested by cold in its unemotional sense.

clue.text: Bit with corset strained from childbirth

indicators.note: strained suggests something pulled out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint that a tight corset has been stretched out of shape after having a baby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strained' rearranges BIT and CORSET.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstetric describes anything relating to pregnancy and delivery, so it is the adjective for what comes from childbirth.

clue.text: Winter sportsman, English in mini?

indicators.note: in puts the English letter inside the short skirt

parts.note: a mini is a short skirt, and the word skirt itself is cut short

explanation.surface: A question about whether a winter sports enthusiast who is English would be found in a Mini car.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the car; 'mini' is a very short skirt, so SKIRT is shortened to SKIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A skier is someone who skis, a sportsman of snowy winter slopes.

clue.text: How babes made erotic porn with a bum

indicators.note: bum as an adjective means bad or false, so the letters are put wrong

explanation.surface: A cheeky description of how babies come about, involving pornography and a backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bum' is the anagram signal, in its sense of wrong or faulty; it rearranges EROTIC PORN and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Procreation is the producing of offspring, which is how babies come to be made.

clue.text: Fruit tree polled containing pea, say

indicators.note: containing means the cut tree holds the letter inside it
polled means beheaded, as a tree with its top cut off, losing the first letter

parts.note: the maple is a tree
the letter P is pronounced like the word pea

explanation.surface: A gardener's note about a fruit tree whose top has been cut, with peas growing inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'polled' takes the head off MAPLE, leaving APLE, which contains P.
explanation.definitionFit: An apple is a common fruit grown on orchard trees.

clue.text: Insultingly, one declining to earn a crust?

definitions.meaning: an insulting name for someone who declines to strike
a crust that forms over a wound

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase, but splits: a strikebreaker, insultingly; and a crust, earned by a wound.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an abusive term for a strikebreaker, and also the hard crust over a healing cut.

clue.text: Bar opening trap

parts.note: a bar of soap is also called a cake of soap
a hole is an opening

explanation.walkthrough: 'trap' and the answer are both slang for the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are British slang for the mouth, as in 'shut your trap'.

clue.text: A load of wine on credit, which is necked?

indicators.note: on means the following pieces come after the credit abbreviation

parts.note: a vat holds a large quantity of wine

explanation.surface: A remark about buying a large quantity of wine on tick and drinking it down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'necked' suggests drinking ('necking' wine); here it means worn round the neck.
explanation.definitionFit: A cravat is a scarf-like neckband worn at the throat, so it is a thing for the neck.

clue.text: Short day needed to collect pound, among one copper — or more?

indicators.note: to collect means the short day word gathers the following letters inside it

parts.note: Tue is the abbreviation of Tuesday

indicators.note: among means the pound word sits inside the copper letters

parts.note: PC is a police constable, one copper
a pound is an enclosure for animals, a pen

explanation.surface: A tale of a quick day out collecting cash, money among the coppers, or maybe a little more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one copper' first suggests a penny coin, but it is a police officer here; 'or more?' then defines the answer as a sum larger than one penny.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuppence is two pennies, a little more than a single copper coin, which is what the question hints.

clue.text: Sound of two swallows parting

indicators.note: sound of says the words are said out loud and spelled differently

parts.note: to swallow a story is to believe it, to buy it; two of them make buy buy

explanation.surface: A picture of a pair of birds going their separate ways with a farewell call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallows' looks like birds but is the verb for believing something.
explanation.definitionFit: Bye-bye is an informal farewell said on parting from someone.

clue.text: Dentist finally going in to identify pain that's most sharp

indicators.note: going in means the letter enters the word for identify

parts.note: to see something can mean to identify or spot it

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of Dentist

parts.note: a pest is a nuisance, a pain

explanation.surface: A dentist probing to find which tooth is causing the sharpest pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Steepest means rising most sharply, as of a slope or climb.
